why: A power of two has exactly one set bit, and n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so a positive n is a power of two exactly when n & (n - 1) == 0.
hints: Write 8, 16 and 12 in binary. What do the powers of two have in common?
Exactly one 1-bit. What does n - 1 look like in binary when n has a single 1-bit?
pitfalls: 0 and negative numbers are never powers of two; check n > 0 first.
1 = 2^0 counts as a power of two.
